Madhuvana

Stories from the Ramayana

Madhuvana

The honey-grove, and understanding good news

In everyday English — Sundara Kanda, sargas 61–63

Stories by Eku

How to Read · · BEFORE WE BEGIN

Read it out loud. This story is made to be told. Read slowly, as if you are sitting with everyone at home.

This book is a story of joy. After a long search the vanaras are coming home — and on the way they find a grove of honey. Where joy comes, let laughter into your voice; where Dadhimukha comes, let drama into your voice.

The yellow boxes hold the characters' own words. Change your voice a little as you speak them — Angada young, Jambavan calm, Hanuman laughing, Dadhimukha furious, Sugriva wise.

(Purple hints) tell you where to pause, whisper, or raise your voice. They are for the reader — do not read them aloud.

The green box at the end of each part — Pause and think. Stop there. Ask questions. Let the listeners speak.

The main story of this book is Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda, sargas 61–63 — Madhuvana. Hanuman has returned from Lanka — Sita is found — and the vanara party is going toward Kishkindha. Anything more you may want to know is given separately at the end, in Where This Story Comes From.

Who's Who · · WHO'S WHO

Hanuman — son of the Wind, minister of Sugriva, messenger of Rama. A powerful vanara, light golden-brown fur, long tail, gentle devoted face, saffron dhoti. He is the one who found Sita.

Angada — son of Vali and Tara, young vanara prince, crown prince. Leader of the southern party.

Jambavan — king of the bears, son of Brahma. Wise and patient — the party's eldest adviser.

Dadhimukha — keeper of Madhuvana, Sugriva's maternal uncle. A great vanara warrior, an elder with grey-brown fur. His work is to guard the grove.

Sugriva — king of the vanaras. Warm brown fur, long tail, royal robes, a simple gold crown. He waits on Prasravana mountain with Rama and Lakshmana for the vanaras.

Rama — prince of Ayodhya. Warm dark-brown skin, black hair tied, simple gold jewellery, an upper cloth over his shoulder, bow in hand.

Lakshmana — Rama's younger brother. Like Rama, a little lighter in colour, bow in hand.

1 · Toward Home · · TOWARD HOME

From Mahendra mountain the vanara party set out — toward Kishkindha. Angada led, Hanuman and Jambavan were with him — and hundreds of vanaras followed.

They were happy — very happy! Sita was found! Hanuman had gone to Lanka, seen Sita, spoken with her, and returned with her message.

The vanaras leapt through the sky — as if their hearts too were flying. Jambavan had said — “Now let us go to Rama — and give him the news.” — and everyone had agreed.

On the way — before Kishkindha — lay a grove. A great grove — full of flowers and fruit. The vanaras saw it — and stopped.

That grove was — Madhuvana.

Pause and think — The vanaras are coming home — and leaping with joy. Does the heart fly too when it is happy? And when the work is done — is it right to stop on the way and celebrate?

2 · The Gate of Madhuvana · · THE GATE OF MADHUVANA

Madhuvana was Sugriva's grove — his most beloved grove. It was closed to everyone — no one could enter. It enchanted all beings — full of fruit, flowers and honey.

Dadhimukha always guarded it — Sugriva's maternal uncle, a great vanara warrior. He was the keeper of the grove.

The vanaras saw the grove — and their mouths watered. Honeycombs hung from the trees — great, golden, honey dripping.

The honey-coloured vanaras went to Angada — “Young prince! May we drink the honey?”

Angada asked Jambavan — “Elder, shall we permit the vanaras to drink the honey?”

Jambavan smiled and said — “Permit them — they are heroes, they have found Sita. Today let them drink the honey.”

Angada said — “Go — drink the honey, eat the fruit!” — and the vanaras rushed into the grove.

Pause and think — Madhuvana was closed to everyone — but Angada and Jambavan opened it. Do rules sometimes break for joy? And does a reward come only after the work is done?

3 · The Honey Feast · · THE HONEY FEAST

Hanuman said — “Vanaras! Drink the honey without fear — anyone who stops you, I will stop!”

And then — the vanaras fell upon the honeycombs! One lifted a comb and drank, one ate fruit, one danced, one sang.

The honey was sweet — the fruit was sweet — and the vanaras swayed with joy. Some danced as if they were drunk.

Laughter echoed through the grove. The branches shook, the honeycombs emptied, fruit peels scattered.

Valmiki says — the vanaras, drinking the honey, became as if intoxicated. They forgot — that this grove belonged to someone else.

Pause and think — The vanaras drink honey and dance — does joy sometimes make us forget our limits? And when everyone is happy — does anyone think that this grove belongs to someone else?

4 · Dadhimukha Comes · · DADHIMUKHA COMES

The guards of the grove — Dadhimukha's men — came running. They saw — the vanaras drinking honey, eating fruit, breaking trees!

The guards said — “Stop! This is Sugriva's grove! No one may come here!” — but the vanaras paid them no heed.

The guards tried to stop the vanaras — but the vanaras drove them away — now with a push, now by chasing them.

Then Dadhimukha himself came — full of anger. He scolded the vanaras — “This grove belongs to the king! Why are you wrecking it?”

But the vanaras — drunk with honey — did not listen to Dadhimukha either. They pushed him — scratched him with claws and teeth — and he fell.

Dadhimukha rose — dusted his clothes — and said — “Now I will go to the king! Sugriva himself will punish you all!”

Pause and think — Dadhimukha was guarding the grove — and the vanaras pushed him. Is it right to forget respect for elders in joy? And when someone is doing their work — is it right to stop them?

5 · Angada's Anger · · ANGADA'S ANGER

Dadhimukha tried to stop the vanaras again — but Angada — merry with honey — forgot that Dadhimukha was old, and Sugriva's maternal uncle.

Angada seized Dadhimukha and dashed him to the ground!

Dadhimukha fell — and rose to dust off his clothes. His guards too fled.

Dadhimukha said — “Enough! Now I will go to Kishkindha — to Sugriva! He will tell you the punishment for wrecking the king's grove!”

And he flew into the sky with his guards — toward Kishkindha.

The vanaras went on laughing — little did they know — that this mischief was about to become great news!

Pause and think — Angada dashed Dadhimukha down — was that only mischief — or a mistake? And when we do something wrong in joy — do we realise it later?

6 · The Complaint to Sugriva · · THE COMPLAINT TO SUGRIVA

Dadhimukha reached Kishkindha — where Sugriva, Rama and Lakshmana sat — waiting for the vanaras.

Dadhimukha touched his forehead to Sugriva's feet — and said — “Great king! Madhuvana is wrecked!”

“Great king! In Riksharaja's time too — in Vali's time too — in your time too — this grove was never open to anyone.”

“Today the vanaras have wrecked it — drunk the honey, eaten the fruit — and driven away the guards!”

Lakshmana asked — “What has happened? Who are those vanaras?”

Dadhimukha said — “Great king! Those vanaras — Angada, Hanuman and their companions — they drink honey as if the grove were theirs! And when we stopped them — they struck us!”

Sugriva listened — and on his face there was no worry — but something else.

Pause and think — Dadhimukha has brought a complaint — and Sugriva listens. Does a king grow angry at once on hearing a complaint — or does he first think? And what Dadhimukha said — was it true?

7 · Sugriva Understands · · SUGRIVA UNDERSTANDS

Sugriva heard Dadhimukha's words — and smiled!

He thought — “Why are the vanaras so happy? Why are they drinking honey? Why are they wrecking the grove?”

And then he understood — “If the vanaras are this happy — it means — Sita is found!”

Sugriva said — (joyfully) “Dadhimukha! Rise — do not be afraid! No punishment will come to you — nor to the vanaras!”

“Vanaras this happy have found Sita. Their joy itself is the news!”

Sugriva comforted Dadhimukha — “Go — send Angada, Hanuman and all the others to me without delay. I want to hear Sita's news from them!”

Rama heard this — and his eyes shone. Lakshmana smiled too.

Pause and think — Sugriva heard the complaint — and did not grow angry, he smiled. Is a wise king one who sees the joy behind a complaint? And is joy itself the greatest news?

8 · The News Reaches Rama · · THE NEWS REACHES RAMA

Dadhimukha returned toward Madhuvana — carrying Sugriva's order — “Send Angada and all the others at once!”

The vanara party set out toward Prasravana mountain — where Rama was waiting.

They leapt along — joyfully, singing — for now they were going to give Rama the news — that they had waited months to give.

Rama stood on Prasravana mountain — and saw the vanaras coming from afar.

He said to Lakshmana — “Look — they are coming. And their joy tells us — that Sita is found.”

And now — Rama will hear Sita's whole story from Hanuman.

Pause and think — The vanaras are going to Rama — carrying the news. Is the bearer of news as happy as the hearer of it? And when someone brings good news — does the road itself feel shorter?

Where This Story Comes From · · WHERE THIS STORY COMES FROM

Main source

The main story of this book is Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda, sargas 61–63 — Madhuvana.

Toward home — sarga 61

The vanaras accepting Jambavan's words and setting out from Mahendra mountain toward Kishkindha; Madhuvana falling on the way — this is in sarga 61.

The gate of Madhuvana — sarga 61

Sugriva's Madhuvana — well-protected, difficult to access, enchanting to all beings; its guardian Dadhimukha — Sugriva's maternal uncle, a great warrior; the vanaras asking Angada for permission to drink the honey; Angada asking Jambavan, and Jambavan permitting — this is in sarga 61.

The honey feast — sargas 61–62

Hanuman saying — “Drink the honey without fear, I will stop anyone who objects”; the vanaras drinking the honey and eating sweet fruits; singing and dancing — as if drunk — this is in sargas 61–62.

Madhu — honey or wine?

Valmiki uses the word madhu (honey) — and says the vanaras, drinking madhu, became intoxicated. Some translations call it honey-wine. In this book it is told as honey — and the vanaras' dancing and singing as their joy and merriment.

Dadhimukha comes — sargas 61–62

The guards trying to stop the vanaras and being driven away; Dadhimukha coming in anger and scolding the vanaras; the vanaras scratching him with claws and teeth; Angada dashing Dadhimukha to the ground — this is in sargas 61–62.

The complaint to Sugriva — sargas 62–63

Dadhimukha and the guards going to Kishkindha; Dadhimukha touching his forehead to Sugriva's feet; his complaint — in Riksharaja's, Vali's or Sugriva's time the grove was never open, now the vanaras have wrecked it; Lakshmana asking — this is in sargas 62–63.

Sugriva understands — sarga 63

Sugriva understanding from the vanaras' jubilation that Sita is found; comforting Dadhimukha; ordering Angada and the others to be sent without delay — this is in sarga 63.

The news reaches Rama — sargas 63–64

Sugriva sending Dadhimukha back — this is in sarga 63. Dadhimukha returning to Madhuvana to summon the vanaras, and the party reaching Rama on Prasravana mountain, is in sarga 64 — that part is not told in this book; the story ends at Sugriva's order.

What happens next

The vanara party is reaching Rama — and Hanuman will tell Rama Sita's whole story. That story is in the next books of this series.
